newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW - Sahaviriya blasts cheap imports.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sahaviriya blasts cheap imports.

text.p: Sahaviriya Steel Industries Plc has asked the Thai government to crack down on cheap imports after being forced to to cut its production of hot-rolled coil steel, a senior official said on Wednesday.

Adisak Lowjun, president of Sahaviriya -- Thailand's sole producer of hot-rolled coil steel -- told Reuters in an interview that his company had requested the government act against imports of cheaper metal from abroad.
"Last week our company submitted a request to the Board of Investment to consider imposing a 50 percent surcharge on steel imports. We expect to receive a reply next month," said Adisak.
Thailand currently imposes a 10 percent duty on imported, hot-rolled coil steel.
Adisak said Sahaviriya had filed a separate request to the commerce ministry, urging it to consider pressing for an anti-dumping law to "fight against steel dumped by several countries."
Adisak said Sahaviriya has more than 200,000 tonnes of the metal, worth about two billion baht ($80 million) lying in its warehouse in the southern province of Prachuab Khirikhan.
He said production for this calendar year at the company's only mill would be cut to around 1.3 million tonnes from an earlier projected 1.8 million tonnes.
Although imports of cheap hot-rolled coil steel would probably be lower in 1996 than last year due to a weaker economy, Adisak said Sahaviriya would still be hurt.
"Importers are expected to bring in between 1.2 to 1.3 million tonnes of hot-rolled coil steel in 1996 compared to 1.8 million tonnes last year," Adisak said.
He said countries such as Russia, Ukraine, China, North Korea and Mexico have set steel prices that are around 43 percent cheaper than what they charge in their home markets.
Sahaviriya Steel is now charging $325 per tonne of hot-rolled coil steel, which is about $125 per tonne higher than imports from those countries, Adisak said.
"My company's production has been cut and I don't want to think about falling revenue," he added. "I feel sad every time I think about it."
But he said cuts were better than closing the mill. "We rather continue our production and lose money than close our mill."
The mill is worth more than 14 billion baht and employs about 700 workers.
